$comment: users.messages.get -> GET gmail/v1/users/{userId}/messages/{id}, response Message. Read from the discovery document 2026-10-01. format=full, fixed: Gmail's payload is a MIME tree (payload.parts, each base64url-encoded) that can nest arbitrarily for a multipart message, and decoding that tree into plain text/HTML is real parsing work this connector does not do yet -- the same class of gap as Drive's file upload, noted rather than rushed. `snippet` (Gmail's own short preview) and `payload.headers` (From/To/Subject/Date, unparsed) cover a lot of practical use without it. `data.payload` itself is still published, raw, for a host that wants to decode the MIME tree on its own side.
title: Gmail message
description: Read one message's headers and preview. The body's plain/HTML text is NOT decoded -- see the raw payload for that.

config.label: Message ID
config.description: From message_list, or another node's output.

outputShape.description: The thread this message belongs to.
System and user label ids currently on this message.
Gmail's own short plain-text preview of the body -- a few hundred characters, not the whole message.
Unix epoch MILLISECONDS, as a string -- when Gmail received it, which can differ from the Date header.
Every RFC 2822 header as { name, value }, unparsed. From/To/Subject/Date live here.

The full MIME tree, raw -- mimeType, body (base64url in body.data for a leaf part), and nested parts for a multipart message. Decode it yourself for plain-text or HTML content; this connector does not flatten it.
Which estate this ran against. Google has no sandbox, so: fake or live.
